title: The Hall of Doors: a short play script
subject: English
source: Written for english/y4 lesson 19 (Teacher's short script: The Hall of Doors (a scene adapted from Alice, chapter 1, written for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 19. A scene adapted from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (Lewis Carroll, 1865), chapter 1. Label the features of a play script.

passage.title: The Hall of Doors
paras: CAST: ALICE, a curious girl. THE WHITE RABBIT, always in a hurry.
SCENE 1: A long, low hall lit by a row of lamps. Doors line both walls. In the middle stands a little three-legged table made of glass.
(The WHITE RABBIT hurries across the stage, looking at a pocket watch.)
WHITE RABBIT: Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting! (He disappears through a door.)
ALICE: (running in, out of breath) Wait! Please wait! (She stops and looks around.) Gone. And every one of these doors is locked.
(ALICE tries the doors one by one, rattling each handle.)
ALICE: (sadly) How shall I ever get out again? (She notices the glass table.) Oh! A tiny golden key.
(She picks it up and tries it in each large door. It fits none of them. Then she pulls back a low curtain and finds a door about fifteen inches high.)

ALICE: (kneeling) It fits! (She unlocks the little door and peers through.) A garden, the loveliest garden I ever saw, with bright flowers and cool fountains. But I could not even get my head through the doorway.
(ALICE stands, sighs and walks slowly back to the table.)
ALICE: (to herself) Perhaps there is another key, or a book of rules for shutting people up like telescopes. (She looks closely at the table.) That was not here before...
passage.source: Adapted for TGA from Lewis Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), which is out of copyright.

checklist: Character name in capitals before each line
Stage directions in brackets, present tense

questions.q: Turn this into a script line: "Oh dear," sighed Alice, sitting down.
Why are there no inverted commas in a script?
questions.a: The character's name shows who is speaking, so speech marks are not needed.
